guide.summary: 要…了, 快…了, 快要…了 and 就要…了 all say that something is about to happen. The 了 at the very end of the sentence is part of the pattern: it marks the new situation that is arriving, not a finished action. The four are close in meaning; what you have to decide is whether there is a specific time word (then use 就要), whether a noun or number follows directly (then use 快), and whether the 了 belongs at all.

subs.label: 了 closes the pattern
subs.focus: Supply the final 了 after 快 / 快要 / 就要 / 要 + verb or adjective, placed at the very end, after any object (快要到北京了). Classic mistakes: dropping 了 (火车快要开) or putting it between verb and object (快要到了北京). Cloze: 了 against ∅, 过, 着, 的; order: where the 了 tile goes.

subs.label: Specific time: 就要…了
subs.focus: With a specific time or countdown (明天, 八点, 还有五分钟) choose 就要, not 快 / 快要. Classic mistake: 我们明天快要考试了. Also test the no-time-word case, where 快 / 快要 is fine. Wrong options here must be 快 or 快要 only: plain 要…了 with a time word (他明天要走了) is acceptable, so never mark 要 wrong.

subs.label: 快 + noun / number + 了
subs.focus: Put 快 directly before a clock time, age, date, festival or amount, with no verb, and end with 了: 快十点了, 我快二十岁了. Classic mistakes: adding 是 (快是十点了), dropping 了 (快十点), using 很快 or 几乎. Never offer 要, 就要 or 快要 as wrong options here; natives accept them variably before a number.

subs.label: Where the adverb goes
subs.focus: Order and rewrite items: 快 / 快要 / 要 / 就要 go after the subject, directly before the verb; a time word precedes 就要 (before or after the subject); 马上 precedes 就要. Classic mistakes: 快 before the subject (快我们毕业了), time word after 就要 (我们就要明天考试了), 快 after the verb (我们到快了).

subs.label: 要 without 了: want / will / should
subs.focus: Decide whether a 要 sentence takes final 了. A wish, a plan or prediction for a stated later time, or advice (want, will, should) takes no 了; something just about to happen does. Classic mistakes: 我要一杯咖啡了; reading 我要回国了 as 'I want to go home'. The English cue must fix the meaning.

subs.label: About to vs. already happened
subs.focus: Choose between about-to and plain 了 for what has already happened or started: 他要走了 (still here) vs 他走了 (gone), 要下雨了 vs 下雨了. Classic mistakes: reading every 了 as past, or 要…了 with a past time word (昨天要下雨了). Each item needs a clue (昨天, 已经, a second clause) that forces one reading.

subs.label: Questions and 'not yet'
subs.focus: The pattern has no negative form. The learner must ask with 吗 at the end, after 了 (快到了吗), and answer in the negative with 还没…呢 or 还有 + time. Classic mistakes: negating the pattern with 不 or 没 (我不快到了, 火车没要开了) and putting 吗 before 了. Keep this sub-point to a small share of a batch.

rules.rule: To say something is about to happen, put 快, 快要, 要 or 就要 before the verb or adjective and end the sentence with 了. With 快, 快要 and 就要 the sentence is wrong without 了.
rules.pattern: Subject + 快 / 快要 / 要 / 就要 + Verb or Adjective + 了

examples.py: yào xià yǔ le
examples.en: It's about to rain.

examples.py: huǒ chē kuài yào kāi le
examples.en: The train is about to leave.

examples.py: tiān kuài hēi le
examples.en: It's almost dark.

examples.py: wǒ de shǒu jī kuài méi diàn le
examples.en: My phone is about to run out of battery.

rules.note: Bare 要 without 了 is still a correct sentence, but it means 'will' or 'want to', not 'about to' (see the plain 要 rule).

rules.rule: If the verb has an object, 了 goes after the object, at the very end of the sentence. Never put it between the verb and the object in this pattern.
rules.pattern: Subject + 快 / 快要 / 要 / 就要 + Verb + Object + 了

examples.py: wǒ men kuài dào běi jīng le
examples.en: We're almost in Beijing.

examples.py: tā men kuài yào jié hūn le
examples.en: They're about to get married.

examples.py: jiě jie jiù yào shàng dà xué le
examples.en: My older sister is about to start university.

rules.rule: When the sentence names a specific time or a countdown, use 就要…了. 快…了 and 快要…了 already mean 'soon' in a vague way and do not combine with a specific time.
rules.pattern: Subject + time word + 就要 + Verb + 了

examples.py: wǒ men míng tiān jiù yào kǎo shì le
examples.en: We have our exam tomorrow.

examples.py: tā xià gè yuè jiù yào huí guó le
examples.en: He's going back to his country next month.

examples.zh: 还有五分钟就要下课了。
examples.py: hái yǒu wǔ fēn zhōng jiù yào xià kè le
examples.en: Class ends in five minutes.

rules.note: Plain 要…了 is also heard with a time word (他明天要走了). 就要 is the safe choice and adds the feeling 'as soon as that'; only 快 and 快要 are wrong here.

rules.rule: With no time word, 快, 快要, 要 and 就要 are all possible. 马上 (right away) is not a specific time; it goes before 就要 or 要.
rules.pattern: Subject + 马上 + 就要 + Verb + 了

examples.py: fēi jī mǎ shàng jiù yào qǐ fēi le
examples.en: The plane is about to take off any moment.

examples.zh: 快要放假了，你打算去哪儿？
examples.py: kuài yào fàng jià le nǐ dǎ suàn qù nǎ r
examples.en: The holidays are almost here. Where do you plan to go?

examples.py: chūn tiān jiù yào lái le
examples.en: Spring is just around the corner.

rules.rule: For 'it's almost + time / age / date / amount', put 快 directly before the noun or number and end with 了. No verb and no 是 is needed.
rules.pattern: (Subject) + 快 + time / number / noun + 了

examples.py: kuài shí diǎn le wǒ děi huí jiā le
examples.en: It's almost ten; I have to go home.

examples.py: wǒ nǚ ér kuài wǔ suì le
examples.en: My daughter is almost five.

examples.py: tā xué zhōng wén kuài sān nián le
examples.en: He has been learning Chinese for almost three years.

examples.py: kuài chūn jié le dà jiā dōu hěn máng
examples.en: It's almost Spring Festival and everyone is busy.

rules.note: 快要 can also stand before a number (快要十点了). 要 and 就要 normally take a verb such as 到 (就要到春节了), though you will hear them directly before a number in speech. In the drills, use 快.

rules.rule: The about-to word is an adverb: it comes after the subject and directly before the verb or adjective. A time word comes before 就要, never after it.
rules.pattern: Subject + (time word) + 快 / 快要 / 就要 + Verb + 了

examples.py: wǒ men kuài bì yè le
examples.en: We're about to graduate.

examples.py: mā ma kuài huí lái le
examples.en: Mum will be back soon.

examples.zh: 明天我就要离开上海了。
examples.py: míng tiān wǒ jiù yào lí kāi shàng hǎi le
examples.en: I'm leaving Shanghai tomorrow.

rules.note: The time word may stand before or after the subject (明天我就要… / 我明天就要…); both are correct, so order items must list both.

rules.rule: 要 with no 了 at the end means want, will or should. Use it for wishes, for plans and predictions at a stated later time, and for advice. Add 了 only when the thing is about to happen.

examples.py: wǒ yào yī bēi kā fēi
examples.en: I'd like a cup of coffee.

examples.py: wǒ míng nián yào qù zhōng guó xué xí
examples.en: I'm going to study in China next year.

examples.py: nǐ yào duō hē shuǐ
examples.en: You should drink more water.

examples.py: wǒ yào huí guó le
examples.en: I'm about to go back to my country.

rules.note: 要 + noun (我要一杯咖啡) can only mean 'want'; it never takes the about-to 了.

rules.rule: 了 alone after a verb or at the end of a sentence says the thing has happened or has started. Add 要 / 快 / 就要 in front and the same sentence says it has not happened yet but is close.
rules.pattern: Verb + 了 (happened) / 要 + Verb + 了 (about to)

examples.zh: 他要走了，你快去跟他说再见。
examples.py: tā yào zǒu le nǐ kuài qù gēn tā shuō zài jiàn
examples.en: He's about to leave; go and say goodbye to him quickly.

examples.py: tā yǐ jīng zǒu le
examples.en: He has already left.

examples.zh: 电影快开始了，我们进去吧。
examples.py: diàn yǐng kuài kāi shǐ le wǒ men jìn qù ba
examples.en: The film is about to start; let's go in.

examples.py: wài miàn xià yǔ le dài shàng sǎn ba
examples.en: It's raining outside; take an umbrella.

rules.note: The about-to pattern looks forward from now, so it does not go with past time words such as 昨天 or 上个星期, or with 已经 before 要.

rules.rule: Ask by adding 吗 after the final 了. The pattern cannot be negated with 不 or 没: for 'not yet' say 还没…呢, or say how long is left with 还有….
rules.pattern: Subject + 快 + Verb + 了 + 吗 / Subject + 还没 + Verb + 呢

examples.py: nǐ kuài dào le ma
examples.en: Are you nearly there?

examples.py: wǒ hái méi dào ne
examples.en: I'm not there yet.

examples.py: fàn kuài hǎo le ma
examples.en: Is dinner almost ready?

examples.py: lí kǎo shì hái yǒu liǎng gè yuè ne
examples.en: The exam is still two months away.

right.py: huǒ chē kuài yào kāi le
right.en: The train is about to leave.

contrasts.why: 快要 needs the final 了 to complete the pattern; without it the sentence is unfinished.

right.py: wǒ men kuài yào dào běi jīng le
right.en: We're about to arrive in Beijing.

contrasts.why: The 了 of this pattern goes at the end of the sentence, after the object. 到了北京 would mean the arrival is already complete, which clashes with 快要.

right.py: wǒ men míng tiān jiù yào kǎo shì le

contrasts.why: 明天 is a specific time, so 就要 is needed. 快要 already means 'some time soon' and does not combine with a specific time.

right.py: xiàn zài kuài shí diǎn le

contrasts.why: 快 goes directly before the time; Chinese needs no 是 for 'it is almost ten'.

right.py: wǒ men kuài bì yè le

contrasts.why: 快 is an adverb and stands after the subject, directly before the verb. English 'soon we graduate' cannot be copied.

contrasts.wrong: 我们就要下个星期搬家了。

right.zh: 我们下个星期就要搬家了。
right.py: wǒ men xià gè xīng qī jiù yào bān jiā le

contrasts.why: The time word comes before 就要, and 就要 stays right in front of the verb.

contrasts.wrong: 服务员，我要一杯咖啡了。

right.py: fú wù yuán wǒ yào yī bēi kā fēi
right.en: Waiter, I'd like a cup of coffee.

contrasts.why: Here 要 means 'want' and is followed by a noun. The about-to 了 only goes with 要 + verb for something that is about to happen.
要…了 looks forward from now and means 'about to rain'. For something that happened yesterday, use the verb with 了 and no 要.
快…了 has no negative form. 'Not yet' is 还没 + verb, usually with 呢.

cheat: About to happen? Check the end of the sentence: 了 must be there, after any object.
Specific time or countdown in the sentence (明天, 八点, 还有五分钟)? Use 就要…了, not 快 or 快要.
Number, clock time, age or festival straight after it? 快 + noun + 了, with no 是.
快 / 快要 / 就要 go after the subject, right before the verb; the time word goes before 就要.
要 with no 了 means want, will or should; 要 + noun is always 'want'.
了 without 要 or 快 means it has already happened or started. Past time word? No 要…了.
Not yet? 还没…呢. Never 不快 or 没要.
